chapter: Chicago, the Marable boats and Marge's St. Louis family band
title: Marge's nurse training and her brother putting her in the band
summary: Marge quit nurse training after a quarrel with a supervisor, so her brother Charlie made her play piano in his dance band, starting at the Almac dance hall.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So when I finished high school I wasn't doing anything, and my sister was going to college. I didn't want to go to college, I didn't want to be a school teacher or anything like that, and it was so hard on my mother sending my sister to college, I didn't want nobody to work that hard for me. And so I went into nurse training, and I took

nurse training for two and a half years, had only a half a year to finish nurse training. And then I got mad with the supervisor of nurses, came home, and I wouldn't finish there. And they said if I would come back and apologize to the supervisor, you know, I could go back in. I only had six more months to finish. And I wasn't going to apologize to anybody, I was a young militant, I guess.

Yeah, a real early militant because I just wasn't going to bow down for anything. So then my brother said -- he told my mother I had to do something, and he wasn't going to have me hanging around doing nothing and he was going to put me to work playing piano, and I cried. With his band. Oh, I cried. I couldn't play that good, he said well you're going to play, you're going to practice and you're going to play. You don't want to do anything, you've got to work, you've got to help mama. So he put me to work and I could read. In those days you had to read the orchestrations. (Unintelligible) as good as all piano players, and so I worked with him and his dance band. The first job I had was playing at the dance hall called Almac in St. Louis.
He put me to work in the band and he said play, you're going to play, take the music and just play with the band. And I played
with the band, and boy, the time I was crying and --
